REGISTERED NO. DL—(N)04/0007/2099
THE GAZETTE OF INDIA
EXTRAORDINARY
THE SAMPLE DATA PROTECTION ACT, 2099
AN ACT to provide for the handling of sample personal data and for matters connected therewith.
BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fiftieth Year as follows:—
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
Short title and commencement.
1. (1) This Act may be called the Sample Data Protection Act, 2099.
(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may notify.
Definitions.
2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) "Board" means the Sample Protection Board;
(b) "child" means an individual who has not completed eighteen years of age;
(c) "personal data" means any data about an individual who is identifiable.
CHAPTER II
OBLIGATIONS OF DATA FIDUCIARY
Notice.
3. (1) Every request for consent shall be accompanied by a notice informing the person of the personal data collected and the purpose of processing.
(2) The notice shall be available in English or any language listed in the
Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—
Consent.
4. (1) Consent shall be free, specific, informed and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action.
(2) The person may withdraw consent at any time, with ease comparable to giving it, and the withdrawal shall not affect processing done before it.
General obligations of Data Fiduciary.
5. (1) A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach.
(2) In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give intimation of the breach to the Board and to each affected person, in the form and manner prescribed.
(3) A Data Fiduciary shall erase personal data—
(a) when the person withdraws consent; or
(b) as soon as the purpose is no longer served,
unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law. The period of 12
months in rule 4 applies to certain classes.
(i) this is a sub-clause and not a new clause;
(ii) so is this.
3
Processing of personal data of children.
6. (1) A Data Fiduciary shall obtain verifiable consent of the parent before processing personal data of a child.
(2) A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children.
CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF DATA PRINCIPAL
Right to access information.
7. A person shall have the right to obtain a summary of personal data processed and the processing activities undertaken.
Right of grievance redressal.
8. (1) A person shall have the right to readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary.
(2) The Data Fiduciary shall respond to grievances within the period prescribed.
Transfer outside India.
9. The Government may, by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data to any country or territory outside India.
THE SCHEDULE
(See section 9)
1. Breach of the obligation to take reasonable security safeguards: may extend to two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
2. Breach of the obligation to give intimation of a personal data breach: may extend to two hundred crore rupees.
